concept.title: Relationships between tasks
concept.shortdesc: A relationship says how one task drives another. Each has one of the three types project plans use:

strow.stentry: The task starts after the other finishes
From the other's end to the task's start
The task starts no earlier than the other starts
The task finishes no earlier than the other finishes

conbody.p: Under Relationships in a task's panel, choose a type and then the task that drives this one. A task can have several relationships, one to each task that drives it, so two tasks can together decide when a third starts: Build the prototype can wait for Wheel guard design and for Electronics to finish. Change a relationship's type in its row, or remove it with the cross.

OpenV does not move a task when its dates break a relationship. It marks the relationship Broken, draws its arrow dashed and red, and leaves the dates to you. A relationship to a task that is done is never broken. A relationship cannot be added to a task that this one already drives, since the two would wait on each other.
